newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks seen easing on HSBC weakness in London.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen easing on HSBC weakness in London.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to drift lower on Friday after HSBC Holdings closed easier in London and buyers take a breather, brokers said.
HSBC fell about HK$5.50 to HK$273.50 in London overnight after closing at an all-time high of HK$279.00 in Hong Kong.

"HSBC jumped so sharply recently and, with a number of covered warrant issues on the stock launched on Thursday, profit-taking is expected today," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
On Thursday, the Hang Seng Index soared 260.27 points, or 1.69 percent, to a record close of 15,706.29 on HSBC's strength.
HSBC's surge in Hong Kong was prompted by expectations of good earnings when the bank announces its interim results on August 4, brokers said.
"The Hang Seng's performance very much depends on HSBC these days," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Selective buying was expected in individual H-shares and red chips, while property counters should move sideways on a lack of good news, Mak said.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index eased 64.10 points, or 0.41 percent, to 15,642.19 on Thursday.
